public_rationale: The 'anyone' clause is contradicted under its ordinary broad reading: a primary survey of 2024 professional non-users found that some identified cost as influencing their non-adoption. Cost was a minority concern, so this does not establish that it was the main market barrier. The DeepSeek functionality clause remains unresolved. R1's reported parity on reasoning tasks is insufficient to prove complete functional equivalence. This proposal rejects the blanket cost assertion, not both clauses.
limitations: The result depends on including professional non-adoption and broader costs; a strictly API-price-only reading remains unresolved.
The survey was published after the post but measures 2024 behavior.
The sample represents arbitrators, not the whole business population.
The functionality clause is not scored as supported or contradicted.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No one has stayed out of generative AI because of cost, and DeepSeek's cheaper models add no new functionality.

statement.excerpt: I don’t think anyone has been “on the sidelines” of generative AI due to costs, (and remember, few seemed to be able to come up with a great use case for o1 or other reasoning models), and DeepSeek’s models, while cheaper, don’t have any new functionality.

from_speaker: I don’t think anyone has been “on the sidelines” of generative AI due to costs
DeepSeek’s models, while cheaper, don’t have any new functionality
our_interpretation: Treat 'I don’t think' as a qualified factual assessment.
'Has been' describes adoption history through publication; no starting date is supplied, so the target period has an open beginning.
The ordinary reading of 'anyone' includes professional users and independent practitioners deciding whether to adopt generative AI.
Costs need to contribute materially to non-adoption; the sentence does not say they must be the only reason.

The functionality clause concerns DeepSeek models available by January 29, 2025. New functionality means a new user-facing capability relative to existing alternatives, not merely lower prices or a different training method.
The parenthetical about a 'great use case' supplies no objective standard and is not treated as a separate measurable assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence supporting both the absence of cost-related non-adoption and the absence of new user-facing functionality in the contemporary DeepSeek models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented non-adopters who identify costs as a reason contradict the first clause. A demonstrated new user-facing capability contradicts the second. A contradiction of one clause does not establish the status of the other.

evidence.publisher: Harry C. Katz and Mark D. Gough / National Academy of Arbitrators
evidence.explanation: In the 2024 survey, some professional non-users identified cost as influencing non-adoption. March 9 is a conservative public-availability date established by Cornell's announcement of the February report, not a claimed exact first-publication date.

This supports the narrower point that R1 addressed reasoning tasks already served by another model. Comparable benchmark performance does not prove that every user-facing function was already available elsewhere.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Company-level evidence isolating model prices would address the narrower reading. A dated, comprehensive feature comparison would resolve the functionality clause.
